column2: The narration as printed in this edition omits two clauses found in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim—«ومن ستر مسلما ستره الله في الدنيا والآخرة» (“whoever conceals [the faults of] a Muslim…”) and «وحفتهم الملائكة» (“the angels surround them”)—although the vocabulary and commentary discuss them. The translation follows the printed text.

On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Whoever relieves a believer of one of the distresses of this world, Allah will relieve him of one of the distresses of the Day of Resurrection;
whoever makes things easy for someone in hardship, Allah will make things easy for him in this world and the Hereafter. Allah helps the servant
as long as the servant helps his brother. Whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, Allah will make easy for him thereby a path to Paradise.

No people gather in one of the houses of Allah, reciting the Book of Allah and studying it among themselves, except that tranquillity descends upon them, mercy covers them, and Allah mentions them among those who are with Him. And whoever is held back by his deeds will not be hastened forward by his lineage.” Reported by Muslim.

Naffasa (“relieves”): removes and dispels. Kurbah (“distress”): great hardship. “Whoever makes things easy for someone in hardship”: by granting him respite until he is at ease. “Allah will make things easy for him”: his affairs, what he seeks and his aims. “Whoever conceals [the faults of] a Muslim”: one not known for harm or corruption, and does not tell anyone of the bad deed he fell into. Yaltamisu (“seeking”):

looking for knowledge of the Sharīʿah, intending by it the Face of Allah. “The houses of Allah”: the mosques. Al-sakīnah (“tranquillity”): calm. “Mercy covers them”: enfolds them from every side. “And the angels surround them”:

encircle them. “And Allah mentions them”: praises them, “among those who are with Him”: of the angels. Baṭṭaʾa (“is held back”): falls short. “Will not be hastened forward by his lineage”: it will not bring him to the ranks of the righteous.
The virtue of one who relieves his Muslim brother of a distress or one of the calamities.
The virtue of meeting the needs of the Muslims and benefiting them with whatever a person can, by himself, his wealth and his words.
Encouragement to conceal the faults of a Muslim who is not by nature of bad character, while advising him to give up his sin.
The recompense may be of the same kind as the deed, as in the hadith.
A person should help his brother to undertake things that are good for him, or that he is continuing in and finds hard.
The virtue of occupying oneself with seeking knowledge and travelling for it from one land to another.
The virtue of gathering in the mosques to recite and study the Qurʾān together, since mercy encompasses them and the angels are present with them.
Might, honour and happiness come through righteous deeds, not through lineage and noble descent.
The mosques are called the houses of Allah.
The believer is exposed to calamities and to bearing hardships for the sake of what benefits him.

This noble hadith teaches us that whoever relieves a Muslim of a distress, makes easy for him something difficult, or conceals a slip or lapse of his that is not known, Allah will recompense him with the same kind of deeds by which he benefited [others]; and that Allah the Exalted helps the servant with His enabling in this world and the Hereafter when he helps his Muslim brother in his difficult affairs;

and that whoever takes a physical path, such as walking to gatherings of remembrance or to the gatherings of meticulous scholars who act on their knowledge, wanting to learn, and takes the figurative path that leads to acquiring this knowledge—revising it, reading, reflecting and understanding the beneficial knowledge imparted to him, and so on—

whoever takes this path with a sincere and righteous intention, Allah will grant him success in beneficial knowledge that leads to Paradise; and that those gathered in one of the houses of Allah to recite and study the Mighty Qurʾān,

Allah gives them tranquillity, enfolding mercy, the presence of the angels and praise from Allah in the highest assembly; and that honour, all honour, lies in righteous deeds, not in lineage and noble descent. Among what has been said on this meaning:
Learn, for no one is born a scholar, / and the one with knowledge is not like one who is ignorant.
The great man of a people who has no knowledge / is small when the assemblies gather around him.
Another poet:
There is no glory in decayed bones; / the glory belongs to the one who keeps glory alive by himself.
Another poet:
Men are only [strong] through their brothers, / as the hand is through the forearm, like the fingers.
Friendship obliges helping one another, / and affection requires supporting one another,
especially in severe misfortunes / and great, rare trials.
